subproblem.title: Consequences of the fibre area identity: finiteness, integrability, signed and box identities
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ 2) with weight μ := R.measure = θ·H²⌞M (H² = μHE[2]), Q a 2-dimensional linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π = Q.starProjection, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, and s ∈ ℝ. Put T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x with orthogonal projection p_{T_x}, Ax := ⟨x,a⟩e − ⟨x,e⟩a, G(x) := |p_{T_x}(Ax)|²/|πx|² (real division, t/0 = 0), f(x) := arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩), F̃(x) := (|x|, f(x)), Z(s,s') := {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|} and Z := Z(s,s). Let H : ℝ² → [0,∞] be a.e.-measurable for Lebesgue measure with ∫ b(p)H(p) dp = ∫_Z b(F̃(x))·ofReal(G(x)) dμ(x) for every Borel b : ℝ² → [0,∞]. Then (i) H(p) < ∞ for a.e. p; (ii) H_ℝ := toReal∘H is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ²; (iii) for every Borel b : ℝ² → ℝ with sup|b| < ∞, ∫ b(p)H_ℝ(p) dp = ∫_Z b(F̃(x))G(x) dμ(x) (Bochner integrals); (iv) for every s' ≤ s, ∫_{(1−s',1+s')×(−s',s')} H(p) dp = ∫_{Z(s,s')} ofReal(G) dμ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 2) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (s : ℝ) (H : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → AEMeasurable H volume → (∀ b : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable b → ∫⁻ p : ℝ × ℝ, b p * H p = ∫⁻ x in {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a ∧ |‖x‖ - 1| < s ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s ∧ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s * ‖x‖}, b (‖x‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)) * ENNReal.ofReal (‖(approxTangentPlane 2 R.carrier x).starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a)‖ ^ 2 / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure) → (∀ᵐ p : ℝ × ℝ, H p ≠ ∞) ∧ Integrable (fun p : ℝ × ℝ => (H p).toReal) ∧ (∀ b : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ, Measurable b → (∃ M : ℝ, ∀ p, |b p| ≤ M) → ∫ p : ℝ × ℝ, b p * (H p).toReal = ∫ x in {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a ∧ |‖x‖ - 1| < s ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s ∧ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s * ‖x‖}, b (‖x‖, Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)) * (‖(approxTangentPlane 2 R.carrier x).starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a)‖ ^ 2 / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure) ∧ ∀ s' : ℝ, s' ≤ s → ∫⁻ p in Ioo (1 - s') (1 + s') ×ˢ Ioo (-s') s', H p = ∫⁻ x in {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a ∧ |‖x‖ - 1| < s' ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s' ∧ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s * ‖x‖}, ENNReal.ofReal (‖(approxTangentPlane 2 R.carrier x).starProjection (inner ℝ x a • e - inner ℝ x e • a)‖ ^ 2 / ‖Q.starProjection x‖ ^ 2) ∂R.measure
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 (area identities, parts (a) and (b)) and the first half of step 8 of the parent-supplied proof of idtp_cse_flux_density_eq. Lebesgue measure on ℝ² is volume on ℝ × ℝ; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal, toReal = ENNReal.toReal.
1. (Frame bound: G ≥ 0 everywhere and G ≤ 1 on {⟨x,a⟩ > 0}.) G ≥ 0 as a quotient of squares. Let ⟨x,a⟩ > 0 and y := πx. Since π is self-adjoint and πa = a, πe = e (a, e ∈ Q; Submodule.inner_starProjection_left_eq_right, Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), ⟨y,a⟩ = ⟨x,a⟩ and ⟨y,e⟩ = ⟨x,e⟩. Using |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a,e⟩ = 0, |Ax|² = ⟨x,a⟩²|e|² − 2⟨x,a⟩⟨x,e⟩⟨e,a⟩ + ⟨x,e⟩²|a|² = ⟨x,a⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩² (norm_sub_sq_real). Bessel's inequality for the orthonormal pair (a, e): with u := ⟨y,a⟩a + ⟨y,e⟩e, 0 ≤ |y − u|² = |y|² − 2⟨y,u⟩ + |u|² = |y|² − (⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩²), so ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² ≤ |y|². Also y ≠ 0 because ⟨y,a⟩ = ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, so |y|² > 0. An orthogonal projection does not increase norms (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le), hence |p_{T_x}(Ax)|² ≤ |Ax|² = ⟨y,a⟩² + ⟨y,e⟩² ≤ |y|² = |πx|², i.e. G(x) ≤ 1 (div_le_one). (The hypothesis dim Q = 2 is not needed here.) In particular 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 on Z.
2. (Measurability.) (a) x ↦ ⟨x,a⟩, ⟨x,e⟩, |x|, ||x| − 1|, |x − πx| and s|x| are continuous; x ↦ ⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,a⟩ is Borel (quotient of measurable maps), and arctan and |·| are continuous, so f and |f| are Borel and F̃ = (|·|, f) is measurable. Each Z(s,s') is a finite intersection of sets {u < v} with u, v Borel, hence Borel (measurableSet_lt). Each box Sq(s') := (1−s',1+s') × (−s',s') is Borel. (b) G is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞Z: by the sibling tangent_aesm (the accepted theorem Submission.imrep_approxTangent_starProjection_aesm with n = 2, U = univ), x ↦ p_{T_x} is a.e.-strongly measurable for H²⌞M; μ = (H²⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ H²⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so it is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac) and for μ⌞Z (restrict). Evaluation (L, v) ↦ L v is continuous bilinear and x ↦ Ax is continuous, so x ↦ p_{T_x}(Ax) is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞Z (ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂ applied to the identity of the operator space); so is its squared norm, and division by the continuous function x ↦ |πx|² preserves a.e.-measurability (AEMeasurable.div), hence a.e.-strong measurability of the real-valued G.
3. (μ(Z) < ∞.) If x ∈ Z then |x| − 1 ≤ ||x| − 1| < s ≤ |s|, so Z ⊆ K := closedBall(0, 1 + |s|), which is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and Borel. By the definition of R.measure, μ(K) = ∫_K θ d(H²⌞M) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH² (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict, Set.inter_comm), which is finite by the IMRep field locallyIntegrable_mult (K compact, K ⊆ univ). Hence μ(Z) ≤ μ(K) < ∞ and μ⌞Z is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_restrict).
4. ((i).) The hypothesis with b ≡ 1 gives ∫ H = ∫_Z ofReal(G) dμ ≤ ∫_Z 1 dμ = μ(Z) < ∞ (setLIntegral_mono with the measurable constant 1, using ofReal(G) ≤ 1 on Z from step 1; setLIntegral_const). Since H is a.e.-measurable with finite integral, H < ∞ a.e. (ae_lt_top').
5. ((ii).) H_ℝ = toReal∘H is a.e.-strongly measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_toReal) and nonnegative, and ∫ ofReal(H_ℝ) ≤ ∫ H < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal_le), so H_ℝ has finite integral (hasFiniteIntegral_iff_ofReal) and is integrable. By (i), ofReal(H_ℝ(p)) = H(p) for a.e. p (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal).
6. ((iii) for 0 ≤ β ≤ M.) Let β : ℝ² → ℝ be Borel with 0 ≤ β ≤ M. (a) p ↦ β(p)H_ℝ(p) is integrable (bounded measurable factor times an integrable function: Integrable.bdd_mul) and nonnegative; x ↦ β(F̃(x))G(x) is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ⌞Z (step 2), nonnegative, and bounded by M·1 on Z (step 1), hence integrable for the finite measure μ⌞Z (Integrable.of_bound with ae_restrict_mem). (b) By integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, ∫ βH_ℝ = toReal(∫ ofReal(β(p)H_ℝ(p)) dp) and ∫_Z β(F̃)G dμ = toReal(∫_Z ofReal(β(F̃(x))G(x)) dμ). (c) For a.e. p, ofReal(β(p)H_ℝ(p)) = ofReal(β(p))·ofReal(H_ℝ(p)) = ofReal(β(p))·H(p) (ENNReal.ofReal_mul with β ≥ 0, and step 5). The hypothesis with the Borel function b := ofReal∘β gives ∫ ofReal(β)·H = ∫_Z ofReal(β(F̃(x)))·ofReal(G(x)) dμ = ∫_Z ofReal(β(F̃(x))G(x)) dμ. Hence the two lower integrals in (b) agree, and ∫ βH_ℝ = ∫_Z β(F̃)G dμ.
7. ((iii) in general.) Let b be Borel with |b| ≤ M (so M ≥ 0). Then b⁺ := max(b, 0) and b⁻ := max(−b, 0) are Borel with values in [0, M] and b = b⁺ − b⁻ (max_zero_sub_eq_self). Pointwise bH_ℝ = b⁺H_ℝ − b⁻H_ℝ and b(F̃)G = b⁺(F̃)G − b⁻(F̃)G, and the four functions on the right are integrable by step 6(a); by integral_sub and step 6, ∫ bH_ℝ = ∫ b⁺H_ℝ − ∫ b⁻H_ℝ = ∫_Z b⁺(F̃)G dμ − ∫_Z b⁻(F̃)G dμ = ∫_Z b(F̃)G dμ.
8. ((iv).) Let s' ≤ s and Sq := Sq(s'). Apply the hypothesis to the Borel function b := 1_{Sq} (indicator with value 1): ∫ 1_{Sq}·H = ∫_Z 1_{Sq}(F̃(x))·ofReal(G(x)) dμ. The left side is ∫_{Sq} H (1_{Sq}·H is the indicator of Sq applied to H; lintegral_indicator). On the right, 1_{Sq}(F̃(x)) = 1_{F̃⁻¹(Sq)}(x) and F̃⁻¹(Sq) is Borel (step 2(a)), so the right side equals ∫_{F̃⁻¹(Sq)} ofReal(G) d(μ⌞Z) = ∫_{F̃⁻¹(Sq) ∩ Z} ofReal(G) dμ (lintegral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict). Finally F̃⁻¹(Sq) ∩ Z = Z(s,s'): x ∈ F̃⁻¹(Sq) iff 1 − s' < |x| < 1 + s' and −s' < f(x) < s', i.e. ||x| − 1| < s' and |f(x)| < s' (abs_sub_lt_iff, abs_lt); since s' ≤ s these imply ||x| − 1| < s and |f(x)| < s, so the intersection is exactly {x : ⟨x,a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |f(x)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|} = Z(s,s'). This proves (iv). ∎
proof_key_steps: Self-adjointness of π and Bessel for (a, e): |p_{T_x}(Ax)| ≤ |Ax| ≤ |πx|, so 0 ≤ G ≤ 1 on {⟨x,a⟩ > 0}; G is μ⌞Z-a.e. strongly measurable via the reused tangent-projection measurability theorem and μ ≪ H²⌞M.
Z ⊆ closedBall(0, 1 + |s|) gives μ(Z) < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult); b ≡ 1 gives ∫H ≤ μ(Z) < ∞, so H < ∞ a.e. and toReal∘H is integrable.
For Borel 0 ≤ β ≤ M both sides of the identity with b = ofReal∘β are lower integrals of integrable nonnegative functions; convert them to Bochner integrals and split a bounded signed b = b⁺ − b⁻.
b = 1_{Sq(s')} together with F̃⁻¹(Sq(s')) ∩ Z(s,s) = Z(s,s') for s' ≤ s gives the box identity.

audit.reason: All four conclusions follow. The projection bound and compact containment give finite mass for arbitrary real s; tangent measurability transfers by absolute continuity. Positive/negative parts justify the signed identity, and indicator substitution proves the box identity for every s'≤s.
